mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved in each of the last three weekly readings (-20.7 to -14.0), and trip-making volume leads discretionary outings; the same momentum carries RETAIL_REC from its -19.3 four-week mean toward baseline over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the trailing four-week mean of -19.3 while TRANSIT keeps improving week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES jumped from -21.6 to -9.6 and has held near that level for three readings; a sustained hold above the -10 percent line marks a durable return of office routines that generates repeat weekday retail footfall, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean holds at or above -10 percent for three consecutive readings
failure_condition: WORKPLACES holds at or above -10 percent for three readings while the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC stays below -19.3.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of TRANSIT (-20.7 to -14.0) and WORKPLACES (-21.6 to -9.6) is multiplicative: commuting corridors convert into retail footfall only when trip supply and destination demand recover together, so the paired series predicts a RETAIL_REC gain within two weeks.
failure_condition: In weeks where both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve, RETAIL_REC shows no gain within the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL cooled from 10.9 to 7.3 percent above baseline, meaning fewer person-hours are spent at home; each point of residential decline releases proportionally more out-of-home discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC rises within one week.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls further from 7.3 while the next weekly mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below -17.7.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has climbed to +27.0, its highest reading in the window, signalling renewed household stockpiling; pantry-loading absorbs both budget and trip time that would otherwise fund discretionary categories, so RETAIL_REC stalls or declines over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above +26 percent
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays above +26 percent while the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds -19.3.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS swung from -27.0 to -17.1 in a single week, a rebound consistent with improved outdoor conditions; outdoor-favourable weeks divert leisure trips away from enclosed malls and dining, so RETAIL_REC weakens relative to the parks series within one week.
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds above -17 while the next weekly mean of RETAIL_REC rises above -17.7.

mechanism_narrative: If the PARKS rebound to -17.1 reverses while TRANSIT stalls at or below -14, the configuration reproduces the t-2w to t-1w tightening phase in which RETAIL_REC flattened near -19; joint re-deterioration of outdoor and transit series therefore predicts lower RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean falls back below -25 while TRANSIT improves by less than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: Under that trigger the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC still exceeds -19.3.

mechanism_narrative: Formal easing is visible in the PARKS rebound and the steady TRANSIT climb; as outdoor and transit freedom expands and the grocery stockpiling spike of +27.0 unwinds, household spend rotates back toward discretionary categories, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS improves by more than 5 points week-on-week yet the forward 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not above -19.3.
